body: Altman (1968) manufacturing model: Z = 1.2*(WC/TA) + 1.4*(RE/TA) + 3.3*(EBIT/TA) + 0.6*(Mkt cap/Total liabilities) + 1.0*(Sales/TA). Zones: Z > 2.99 safe; 1.81-2.99 grey; < 1.81 distress (some tables use 1.8/3.0). Z' (private firms, book equity) cut-offs ~1.23/2.90. Z'' (non-manufacturers/emerging markets, drops sales/TA): Z'' = 6.56*X1 + 3.26*X2 + 6.72*X3 + 1.05*X4, distress < 1.1, safe > 2.6 (EM version adds +3.25 constant). Altman's original sample classified ~95% of bankrupts correctly one year ahead, with accuracy falling sharply 2+ years out -- it's a near-term distress gauge, not a fraud detector. Indian use: run on consolidated numbers; exclude banks/NBFCs/insurers (use leverage, ALM, divergence instead); market-value term (X4) can mask distress in bubbles (Adani 2022, Nikola) -- check with book-equity Z'. Low Z examples pre-collapse: Jet Airways (negative RE and WC), Kingfisher, Future Retail, Unitech 2008. A low Z with rising pledges or CP dependence is a disqualifier; a low Z in a cyclical at trough can be a turnaround -- require debt reduction evidence.
title: Altman Z-score: distress cut-offs and Indian usage
